title: Reading performance correctly, and when to switch
objectives: Pick XIRR, CAGR or absolute return for the right case.
Judge a fund against its benchmark and category over 3 to 5 years.
Name valid reasons to switch and what to check first.
body_md:
## Reading performance correctly

| Metric | Use it for | Common mistake |
|---|---|---|
| XIRR | SIPs and multiple investments at different dates | Comparing SIP returns using simple or absolute return |
| CAGR | A single lump-sum investment | Applying it to SIPs |
| Absolute return | Very short periods only | Judging a 5-year holding by total % gain |
| vs Benchmark / Category | Judging the fund manager | Judging a fund on one good or bad year |

## When to recommend switching a fund

- Consistent underperformance vs benchmark and peers over 3+ years, not one bad year
- Change in fund manager or investment style that no longer suits the client
- Change in the scheme's mandate or category
- Change in the client's goal or horizon

Always check exit load and tax before recommending a switch.

> **Investor takeaway:** Starting a SIP is step one. Review yearly, step up with income, and rebalance.
example: A client's SIP shows an absolute gain of 18% after 4 years and she thinks it is poor. XIRR on the staggered instalments is about 11% a year, and the fund is ahead of its benchmark. You advise staying.
say: For a SIP, XIRR is the right measure, because it counts each instalment's date.
One bad year is not a reason to switch. Three years behind benchmark and peers is a reason to review.
never: This fund lost 5% this year, let's switch.
Compare your SIP's absolute return with a lump sum's CAGR.

check.q: Which return measure should be used for a SIP portfolio?
check.why: XIRR accounts for each instalment's date. CAGR is for a single lump sum.

check.q: Which is a valid reason to recommend switching out of a fund?
o: Underperformance vs benchmark and peers over 3+ years
A friend's fund returned 40% last year
check.why: Other valid reasons are a manager/style change, a mandate change, or a change in the client's goal.

check.q: Before recommending any switch, the distributor must always check:
o: The NAV of the new fund
Whether the new fund is an NFO
check.why: A switch is a redemption plus a purchase, so it can trigger exit load and tax.
